fi-poecilia-velifera.title: Sailfin Molly
fi-poecilia-velifera.summary: The giant sailfin molly, Poecilia velifera, is a livebearer endemic to southeastern Mexico, with introduced populations in several other countries. Young fish are hard to tell from P. latipinna, and…
rows: Omnivore. Omnivorous by nature, feeding on a variety of zoobenthos and detritus in the wild.
Endemic to southeastern Mexico but has been introduced into several other countries, including Colombia , Israel , Singapore and Taiwan .
notes: Ideally a heavily-planted setup with some floating cover and areas of open water.
The aquarium should be as large as possible as in small aquariums the development of the males' dorsal may be impaired.

fi-poecilia-latipinna.title: Poecilia latipinna
fi-poecilia-latipinna.summary: The sailfin molly, Poecilia latipinna, is a livebearer native to southern North America and Mexico, from Carolina to Veracruz. Bred into many colour morphs and crossed with P. sphenops, it can live…
rows: Herbivore / algae browser. Wild fish are almost exclusively herbivorous , feeding on algae and other plant material.
Native to Southern North America and Mexico , from Carolina to Veracruz.
notes: A densely planted aquarium with some open space for swimming.
It should be noted that these are highly vegetarian fish so any soft-leaved plants may be destroyed.

fi-poecilia-sphenops.title: Molly
fi-poecilia-sphenops.summary: The short-finned molly, Poecilia sphenops, is a livebearer whose native range runs north from Venezuela and Colombia to Mexico. Many colour morphs exist, including the black molly, and years of…
rows: Omnivore. Omnivorous by nature, feeding on a variety of zoobenthos and detritus in the wild.
It's native range runs north from Venezuela and Colombia to Mexico , with isolated populations on some Caribbean islands.
notes: A planted tank is preferable but this species must be maintained in moderately hard or harder water, with a basic pH.
When kept in soft or acidic water, the fish weakens fairly rapidly, frequently indicated by shimmying, fungus , and/or clamped fins.
